messages:
emma: quick Q — trying to track down logs for request_id=9a7b6c2f. Client saw a 502 and the console trace link only shows spans, no pod logs. anyone know the usual places to check?
sanjay: first quick checks: 1) console Requests search -> paste the req id (try both raw id and x-redwood-request header form). 2) check the ingress / edge pod logs (that’s where the req id is usually injected).

emma: I tried the Requests UI search and nothing showed up. the trace exists (trace-id a1b2c3) but it doesn’t link to logs.
tyler: if trace exists but no logs it usually means the sidecar or log forwarder dropped the req header. try running stern on the suspected pods and grep for the id — faster than waiting for ES indexing.

maya: stern example I use locally:
```
stern "(api|ingress)" -n prod --since 1h | rg 9a7b6c2f || true
```
that will stream recent lines from api or ingress pods and highlight the id.

sanjay: alternative: kubectl logs for the pod that the trace points to (if you can resolve span -> pod). command: 
```
kubectl -n prod logs <pod-name> --container app --since=30m | rg 9a7b6c2f
```
if you only have trace id, use the trace UI to get span.service and span.host, that hints the pod selector.

tyler: we also have a small helper script: `redwoodctl find-logs --request 9a7b6c2f --window 30m` — it runs through edge, proxy, and app pods and returns matching lines (might require SSO).

emma: oh nice — I don’t have redwoodctl locally. is there a fallback?

maya: fallback is elasticsearch/observability index query (if you have Kibana access). query example: 
```
POST /observability-*/_search
{
  "query": { "match": { "request_id": "9a7b6c2f" } }
}
```
but that depends on fields being indexed. indexing lag is the usual cause.

sanjay: if nothing in ES and stern/kubectl find nothing, check the edge/proxy for dropped headers. the header we use is `x-redwood-request-id` or sometimes `x-request-id`. proxy config can strip/overwrite them.

emma: how do I find which proxy pod handled that request? trace span shows service=frontend-proxy, span.host ip 10.2.7.45. any quick mapping from ip -> pod?

tyler: yes: `kubectl get pods -o wide -n prod | rg 10.2.7.45` or `kubectl get pod -o json -n prod | jq '.items[] | select(.status.podIP=="10.2.7.45") .metadata.name'`.

maya: small tip: sometimes requests are routed through edge autoscaler and the final app pod doesn’t log the request id until the response path. check both ingress and app. also look for the header in access logs, not only app logs.

emma: trying stern now...

ops-bot: deploy-bot finished deploy main -> prod (revision f3e1). impacted pods: ingress-7f9b, api-55c2. :white_check_mark:

emma: seeing ingress-7f9b streaming now, found lines with 9a7b6c2f in access log — upstream returned 502. looks like upstream app never logged the body.

sanjay: nice — next step is to check the upstream app pod logs with the time window from the ingress line. if still nothing, check the app’s log level or if it filtered out certain 5xx bodies.

tyler: if you want an end-to-end quick command to share with oncall, I usually send: 
```
# find the pod by ip from span
kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | rg 10.2.7.45
# stream ingress and app logs around time
stern "ingress|api" -n prod --since 10m | rg 9a7b6c2f
```
works 90% of the time.

maya: also add to your incident note: whether the request id came from client or generated at edge. if client-supplied id differs we log both x-request-id and x-redwood-request-id.

emma: thanks all, I’ve gathered enough to open a bug on the upstream service. will post the follow-up with pod lines. :sparkles:
